title: VPC Field Sprint Diary — Weeknotes & Escalations Sep 28–29 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick, informal weeknote covering two-day field sprint focused on Aurora Biomed VPC install and a stubborn network fragmentation issue. This is a working log: notes to self, standup blurbs, triage steps, and action items for follow-up.

Attendees (on-site + remote):
- Avery Chen (rotation lead, on-site)
- Samuel Ortiz (network SME, remote)
- Priya Nair (install engineer, on-site)
- Marcus Lee (SRE/observability, remote)
- Rosa Alvarez (customer success, customer liaison)

High-level summary:
- Deploy finished initial control-plane/k8s provisioning on customer VPC by EOD 2026-09-28.
- Major blocker: intermittent model-serving timeouts traced to MTU fragmentation and path MTU blackhole behavior between customer F5 LB and Redwood inference nodes. Symptoms appeared under sustained batched requests (>16 concurrent streams).
- Mitigation applied: temporary lowering of MTU on inference hosts (9000 -> 1400) + enabling TCP MSS clamp on customer edge. Customer accepted temporary perf hit.
- Next steps: permanent fix requires coordinated changes in customer LB config or our egress encapsulation; plan documented below.

Day 1 — 2026-09-28 (standup snippets):
- 09:15 quick sync: confirm host provisioning, kube nodes in NotReady → fixed by bumping kubelet cgroup limits.
- 11:00 smoke tests: chat flows ok under low load.
- 14:30 load run: 100 concurrent requests -> 3% timeout rate; packet captures show repeated TCP retransmits and 'frag needed' ICMP observations from intermediate device.
- 15:10 escalation call with customer network team: they run F5 LTM 14.x with jumbo frames enabled on internal VLAN; we suspect inconsistent MTU along path. Customer runbook lacks end-to-end MTU verification steps.
- 16:00 workaround applied: set host MTU to 1400 and add iptables rule to clamp MSS to 1360 on host egress. Immediate reduction in retransmits and errors dropped to <0.1%.
- 17:30 retrospective: capture saved to /mnt/field-captures/aurora-09028.pcap (note for Marcus to ingest into observability).

Day 2 — 2026-09-29 (standup snippets):
- 09:00 morning sync: metrics show stable request success but tail latency increased ~40ms due to smaller MTU and extra fragmentation handling. Customer OK with temporary latency but asked for permanent plan.
- 10:30 deep-dive with Samuel: confirmed path MTU blackhole caused by F5 not sending ICMP frag-needed to source; observed an MTU mismatch in cloud provider overlay -> likely due to VXLAN offload + trunking on their top-of-rack.
- 12:00 joint ticket opened with customer's network ops (ticket CN-2758) to review F5 configuration for 'strip-jumbo' / ttl/DF behavior and to validate MTU on internal switches.
- 15:00 proposed long-term options: (A) update customer LB to send proper ICMP or enable MSS clamp on LB; (B) keep host MTU high and change our egress path to avoid encapsulating large packets (requires cloud provider network policy change); (C) add transparent proxy that does MSS clamping at egress in our VPC. Customer prefers A.

Technical forensic notes (concise):
- Observed symptoms: increased retransmits, delayed ACKs, service-level 524-like timeouts at our side.
- Tcpdump excerpt (paraphrased): multiple PSH,ACKs with payloads dropped and no ICMP frag-needed seen by our hosts. ICMP frag-needed only visible from an intermediate switch when we captured mirrored traffic.
- Root cause hypothesis: intermittent MTU mismatch across one of the tenant VLAN trunks; F5 is stripping/repacking frames in a mode that prevents ICMP propagation.
- Temporary mitigation: host MTU=1400 + egress MSS clamp to 1360.

Customer-specific notes (Aurora Biomed):
- They run regulated workloads (PHI adjacent). They requested all changes be logged and any package with root-level commands must be approved by their SecOps.
- Change window for permanent LB config scheduled 2026-10-06 (customer change freeze before then).
- CS asks for a short one-pager that explains the MTU issue in non-technical terms for their Exec. Rosa to draft.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Samuel Ortiz: compile pcap -> upload to observability; add tcp_flow summary and recommended packet-level checks. Due 2026-09-30.
- Marcus Lee: add field-capture ingest pipeline (small parser) to observability so we can correlate packet events with token-level delays. Due 2026-10-07.
- Priya Nair: produce an install checklist update that includes an MTU verification step and documenting how to test path MTU using iperf/tracepath. Draft due 2026-10-04.
- Avery Chen: coordinate with customer SecOps for change window and outcomes; write a 'post-mortem-lite' for this sprint. Due 2026-10-08.
- Rosa Alvarez: draft the executive one-pager and circulate to customer and internal stakeholders by 2026-09-30.

Unresolved questions / parking lot:
- Is this specific to F5 LTM 14.x behavior or seen on other LB vendors? Need a short matrix of observed vendor behaviors for runbook.
- Do we want to add an automated MTU check to our preflight that simulates batch traffic to surface this before install? (priority: high)
- Can we add an option in our node bootstrap to enable MSS clamp automatically when customer indicates their LB does not support ICMP properly?

Runbook / process improvements (for next sprint):
- Add 'path MTU verification' to preflight checklist and SDG (small diagnostic guide) with: tracepath, iperf UDP fragmentation test, tcpdump capture sample, sample iptables mss clamp rule.
- Create a quick KB titled 'MTU blackholes & inference batch workloads' (target audience: Solutions Eng + Customer NetOps). Draft owner: Priya.
- Update private-deployments playbook to include an explicit handoff to customer NetOps for LB jumbo frame settings.

Misc notes to self / raw fragments: 
- Slack thread #private-deployments: see thread ts=2026-09-28T16:12 for customer log snippets.
- Possible follow-up experiment: replicate large-batch failure in lab with an F5 (or haproxy sim) + VXLAN overlay. Assign to Samuel and Marcus as a spike.
- Performance impact estimate: temporary MTU drop cost ~6–12% throughput on large token streams (approx. 1.2–2.4 rps reduction on Aurora baseline).

Closing/next sync:
- Standup Monday 2026-10-04 09:00 PT to review customer LB change results and finalize runbook changes.

-- end of diary entry --

Notes about doc: informal field diary; will convert to a short public-facing KB and internal runbook after customer sign-off.
